title: Patient Authorization for Member-Level Appeals — Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing)
content:
**Policy clause.** On an Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing), Riverbend files a provider-level appeal in its own name without the patient's signature. A member-level appeal (a member appeal with the patient's authorized-representative form, a Medicare Advantage reconsideration or a Medicaid HMO appeal filed for the patient) asserts the patient's own appeal rights and is filed only under the patient's authorization. A member-level appeal requires a signed authorized-representative form of the payer class's accepted form type for that claim, signed no more than the form's validity period before the filing date. The form is sent to the patient for signature through any of the payer class's signature channels and only the patient can sign it; a form that is unsigned, revoked, of the wrong type or older than its validity cannot support the filing. The patient may instead file their own member appeal directly with the payer, in which case Riverbend files nothing at member level.

**What the records must show before a member-level filing**

| Check on the authorization record for that claim | Required |
|---|---|
| Status | signed (not unsigned, not revoked) |
| Form type | the type the payer class accepts |
| Signed date | no more than the validity period before the filing date |
| Claim | the same claim the appeal is filed on |

The patient's statement that they signed something does not replace the signed record.

**Basis questions**
- *Does a provider-level appeal need the form?* No; Riverbend files it in its own name.
- *Can a representative sign for the patient?* No; only the patient can sign the form.
- *What if the patient files directly with the payer?* Riverbend files nothing at member level.
- Example (hypothetical): a correctly typed form signed 400 days before the intended filing date, under a 365-day validity, cannot support the filing.
